paper_metadata.title: Effect of Interpass Temperature on Wire Arc Additive Manufacturing Using High-Strength Metal-Cored Wire

evidence.quote: Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) is suitable to fabricate large components because of its high deposition rate. In this study, a metal-cored low-alloy high-strength welding filler metal was used as feedstock.

attributes.composition: mixture of MnO2 and SiO2 particles

evidence.quote: The black dots were found to be oxide particles using SEM-EDS, as shown in Figure 4b,c. The atomic percentage of the particles shows the ratio of (Mn + Si) to O to be 1:2, indicating they are a mixture of MnO2 and SiO2 particles, which are typically observed in Mn/Si deoxidized steels [24].

The average of the three measurement results was taken as the grain size and were 3.9 ± 0.1 μm, 4.1 ± 0.1 μm, and 4.9 ± 0.2 μm for the interpass temperatures of 150 °C, 350 °C, and 600 °C, respectively.

The fraction of LAGB was measured to be 25.5%, 25.9, and 24.1% for the interpass temperatures of 150 °C, 350 °C, and 600 °C, indicating that the fraction of LAGB or HAGB keeps at the similar level for the different interpass temperatures.
The maximum texture index is 2.9 for the interpass temperature of 150 °C, 3.8 for the interpass temperature of 350 °C, and 3.6 for the interpass temperature of 600 °C.
